Kanye’s St. Petersburg Concerts Reportedly Scrapped — The planned October concerts in Russia of US rapper Kanye West, who sang “I beat up the p***y for Ukraine” in one of his musical compositions, reportedly fell through days after being removed from the official tour schedule, with the planning troubled by venues pulling out and Russian officials criticizing West’s antics soon after they were announced.
Zelensky Says He Would Visit Moscow ‘On a Rocket’ — Zelensky’s reply to Russian reporters in New York echoed a position he made explicit in January: he is willing to meet Putin, but not in Moscow.

‘Needed Every Day’: Zelensky, Rutte Talk Patriots — President Volodymyr Zelensky asked NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte to help secure a winter air defense package after Russia launched three waves of ballistic missiles at Kyiv. Zelensky said Ukraine is improving its defenses against cruise missiles and jet-powered drones, but still relies on Patriot interceptors to counter ballistic threats.

Fire at Polish Starlink Hub Sparks Sabotage Investigation — Poland’s Deputy Prime Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski said a fire at the Wola Krobowska Starlink ground station in central Poland is being treated by authorities as a likely sabotage attempt. The blaze damaged the facility's power systems and temporarily disrupted internet connectivity provided through the station, which serves parts of Central and Eastern Europe and supports communications used by Ukraine.

Ukraine Sent North Korean POWs to South Korea, Zelensky Says — Zelensky said the two North Korean soldiers captured in 2024 departed for South Korea “recently” during his UN speech on Wednesday. The two initially rejected asylum offered by Seoul but reportedly changed their minds close to a year later, with reports in late 2025 suggesting they wanted to live in South Korea.

Russian Radars and Drone Launch Site Damaged by Ukraine — Ukrainian forces struck two Russian radar stations, a facility used to store and launch attack drones near Donetsk, and a fuel depot in the occupied Zaporizhzhia region, the General Staff said. The military did not specify the weapons used or the extent of the damage.

Russia’s Global Recruitment Pipeline: How Russia Hunts the World’s Poor to Feed Its War in Ukraine – Part 2 — The second part of this investigation examines the global reach of Russia’s foreign recruitment campaign, focusing on South Asia, Latin America, Indonesia, and former Soviet states. CIA Warns of Potential Russian Drone Strikes From Shadow Fleet Vessels — According to a report by Spain's El Mundo, the CIA has warned European allies that Russia may be planning to launch drones from shadow fleet vessels in the Mediterranean Sea. The alleged attacks could target countries such as Spain, France, and Italy and form part of a broader pattern of hybrid operations against NATO members supporting Ukraine.

Kremlin Says Too Early to Discuss Putin’s G20 Trip After Welcoming US Invitation — The Kremlin welcomed a US invitation for Russian President Vladimir Putin to attend the G20 summit in Miami on Wednesday, only to walk back its statement on Thursday by saying it was too early to talk about it. The invitation came as Washington pushed for negotiations to end the war, continuing the diplomatic momentum achieved during the early September visit to Moscow and Kyiv by US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared

Ukraine Pushes Forward in 4 Frontline Sectors as Russia Struggles for Gains — Ukrainian forces recently advanced in 4 frontline sectors, including near Kupyansk, Chasiv Yar and two areas of Dnipropetrovsk region, as per ISW. Russian forces also made limited gains near Kostyantynivka and Dobropillya, but failed to advance in northern Kharkiv region.

‘No Other Choice’: Zelensky Warns Russia of Winter Strikes — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Ukraine would make the coming winter “painful” for Russia if Moscow continues striking Ukrainian energy and heating infrastructure. Speaking at the UN General Assembly, he invoked “General Winter” – traditionally viewed as Russia’s ally – and said it could instead help those defending themselves from Russian aggression.

Russia’s Oil Sites Hit Again in Overnight Ukrainian Drone Attack — Russian officials reported damage to an oil depot in the Rostov region and a fire at an unidentified facility in the Krasnodar region. A Ukrainian monitoring channel said the second site was another oil depot.

Russian Envoy Dmitriev Heads to US for Talks With Witkoff, Kushner — Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev is heading to New York for talks with Trump administration officials as Ukraine pushes an unconditional ceasefire backed by 50 countries. Moscow has yet to respond, while US-Russia contacts continue over the war and potential peace talks

Russia Sanctions Lifted for Two Oligarchs — The article criticizes France and the EU over reported efforts to ease sanctions on Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman as part of a diplomatic deal involving Azerbaijan and detained French citizens. Critics, including Yulia Navalnaya, argue the episode shows financial interests taking precedence over principles and support for ordinary Russians.

Zelensky: Ukraine Intercepted 60% of Ballistic Missiles in Overnight Russian Attack — Ukraine intercepted 60% of the ballistic missiles launched during Russia’s latest overnight attack, President Volodymyr Zelensky said. The assault included three waves of ballistic strikes on Ukraine and a drone attack on Kyiv, as Zelensky warned that Ukraine is struggling to replenish its air defense missile stocks.

Russian Attack Damages Medical Facility, Homes and School in Odesa — A Russian overnight attack damaged a medical facility, 10 residential buildings and a school in Odesa, with no casualties reported. The strike came amid a sustained campaign targeting the Black Sea port city, while Kyiv was also hit by Russian ballistic missiles and drones.

Finland, Ukraine Seal Major Drone Deal as Stubb Exposes Russia’s Stalled Donbas Offensive — Finnish President Alexander Stubb told the UN Security Council that Russia’s Donbas push could take years as massive losses barely move the front. Hours later, he and Zelensky signed a Drone Deal expanding joint production, technology transfers, and defense cooperation.

Trump Approval Falls to 33% as Economy Weighs on GOP Ahead of Midterms – CNN Poll — A new CNN poll finds Donald Trump’s approval at its lowest point in CNN polling across his two terms, with economic dissatisfaction emerging as a major issue weeks before the US midterm elections.

Zelensky Urges Strong US Response During Congress Talks as Russian Ballistic Missiles Hit Kyiv — Zelensky said Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv while he was discussing sanctions with US lawmakers in New York. He urged Washington to provide ballistic missile interceptors and implement sanctions against Russia and those helping it earn revenue.

Kyiv Under Attack: Russian Missiles Kill 2, Injure at Least 6 Amid UN Ceasefire Push — Kyiv authorities reported two people killed and at least six injured. Missile debris damaged a maternity hospital, a nearby diagnostic center, and homes across the capital.

‘Tell Your Boss: Enough Is Enough,’ Polish FM Confronts Lavrov at UN — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski confronted Sergey Lavrov at the UN, rejecting Kremlin claims on Ukraine, invoking Russia’s wartime record, and warning Moscow against further escalation.

Moscow’s Ceasefire Bingo Card – What Might the Kremlin Say to Ukraine’s Unconditional Ceasefire? — “It’s Ukraine’s fault,” “Good idea but…” “What if we try something else?” After Ukraine reiterates its plan for an unconditional ceasefire, here’s a list of potential responses from Moscow based on its past remarks on similar proposals.

Zelensky Tells UN Russia Lost Nearly 249,000 Troops This Year — Speaking during the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York on Wednesday, President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia lost nearly 249,000 troops this year to capture just over 1,000 square kilometers (roughly 386 square miles) of Ukrainian territory.

Lavrov Tells UN Security Council Russia Won’t Pause the War During Negotiations — During the United Nations (UN) Security Council, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said that the Kremlin will not pause its “special military operation” even during negotiations. His Ukrainian counterpart, Andrii Sybiha, accused Russia of blocking peace, while 51 countries signed a joint initiative urging Moscow to accept a full ceasefire.

Russian Drone Attacks Kill 2, Injure 62 as Explosions Rock Ukraine Nationwide — Kyiv came under a Russian drone attack Wednesday morning, with at least five explosions reported near the Central Railway Station area. The station itself was not hit, Ukrzaliznytsia said. At least four people were wounded, according to Mayor Vitali Klitschko. Russian strikes have killed two people and injured 43 others just in Kyiv, while the overall casualties toll rose to 62 nationwide.

51 Countries Issue Joint UN Statement Urging Russia to Accept Immediate Ceasefire as Sybiha Condemns Latest Strikes — Fifty-one United Nations (UN) member states issued a joint statement supporting Ukraine, urging Russia to accept an immediate ceasefire, return Ukrainian civilians and protect Black Sea navigation. The appeal came as Russian strikes killed at least two people and injured more than 40 in a sweeping barrage across Ukraine on Wednesday.

Language Lab Turns 10 and Launches ‘Ukraine Connected,’ a Community for Internationals in Ukraine — Kyiv-based Ukrainian language school Language Lab is marking its tenth anniversary by launching Ukraine Connected, a new community for foreigners and Ukrainians who want to be part of modern Ukraine. Founder Ksenia Golubytska says the initiative grows out of the support the school has long given its students, from everyday help to cultural events. Through curated chats, meetups and larger gatherin

Russia Must Answer for Crimes in Crimea, Zelensky Says — Speaking during the sixth International Crimea Platform Summit on Wednesday, Sept. 23, President Volodymyr Zelensky said restoring international law requires Russia to answer for crimes committed in Crimea and other occupied Ukrainian territories. More than 60 participants attended the gathering in New York, including 16 leaders from across the world.

More Range, More Payload: Ukraine’s Race to Build Better Drone Batteries — Ukrainian battery maker PAWELL is developing solid-state and sodium-ion technologies to give drones greater range and payload capacity. The company aims to scale production to 10,000 units a day while localizing its battery supply chain in Ukraine.

Azov Crushes Russian Force, Foils Druzhkivka Encirclement — Ukraine’s Azov Corps said a joint operation eliminated a Russian grouping that had accumulated in the Donetsk region throughout the summer. The corps claimed that 193 Russian troops were killed, 44 wounded and three captured, disrupting plans to encircle Druzhkivka and advance toward Dobropillya.

Russian Strike on Kyiv on Sept. 23: Legendary ‘Puck’ Gutted by Fire — Russian strikes on the capital’s railway infrastructure on Sept. 23 hit the old modernist Zaliznychnyi Market, built in Soviet times. Fire from the strike ravaged the building.

Ukraine Recaptured Almost All Territory Russia Gained in 2026, Zelensky Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia captured approximately 890 square kilometers of Ukrainian territory in 2026, while Ukraine retook around 800 square kilometers on other parts of the front. According to his figures, Moscow achieved a net territorial advantage of only about 100 square kilometers despite suffering heavy losses.

Baltic States Reportedly Seek Urgent €500M EU Aid for Drone Defense — The three Baltic states have asked the European Commission for €500 million ($570 million) to boost their defense against drones, citing the increasing Russian threat, according to a report in Finland’s Iltalehti newspaper on Tuesday.

Taiwan Cement Backs Ukraine’s Recovery With IFCEM Investment — Taiwan Cement Corporation is set to become a strategic investor in PJSC Ivano-Frankivskcement, Ukraine's leading cement producer, through a transaction with the Swiss majority owner CemInWest and the owners of three related companies. The deal, whose value was not disclosed, still needs antitrust and regulatory approvals.

Russian Strikes Hit Major Ukrainian Manufacturers — Russian missile strikes targeted key Ukrainian industrial sites on Tuesday. The attacks hit Interpipe’s steel facility in Dnipro, killing four people and injuring seven. Meanwhile, a separate strike completely destroyed a Snizhna Panda warehouse in the Odesa region.

Confirmed Russian War Dead Top a Quarter Million — The BBC and Mediazona said 258,980 Russian soldiers have been identified by name as killed in Ukraine since 2022, with the actual toll likely doubling that figure. Ukraine estimates 1.52 million Russians killed and wounded, while London puts the number of dead at around 500,000 out of 1.5 million total casualties. Deaths are highest in poorer regions, while recruitment increasingly relies on bonuses and pressure amid low volunteer counts.

Russian Mi-8 Helicopter Briefly Violates Polish Airspace, Poland Scrambles Fighters — A Russian Mi-8 military helicopter briefly violated Polish airspace near Braniewo on Wednesday, prompting Poland to scramble fighter jets. Warsaw called the incident another apparent test of its air-defense readiness. The incursion follows several previous Russian aircraft and drone violations of Polish airspace.

Russia Seeks to Destroy and Depopulate Odesa. Can It Withstand the Pressure? — Odesa has spent many months surviving powerful airstrikes that terrorize the port, economy, infrastructure, and civilian population. What is Russia’s goal, and will Odesa residents
be able to withstand this new wave of Russian terror?

Russian Attack Cuts Kyiv Internet, Delays Trains — A Russian drone attack disrupted internet service for some Kyiv residents after damaging data centers used by two providers. Railway infrastructure was also hit, causing delays of more than nine hours on some routes, although Ukrzaliznytsia stressed that passenger train traffic was not completely suspended.

Ukraine’s New Civil Code Could Let Workers Ignore Work Chats on Weekends — Ukraine’s new draft Civil Code would give workers a “right to informational peace,” allowing them to ignore work-related messages during weekends and other non-working hours. The bill would also introduce a “right to be forgotten” and new protections covering privacy, intellectual property and AI.

NATO Keeps Article 5 Trigger ‘Deliberately Ambiguous’ — NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte said the alliance deliberately avoids defining the precise threshold for activating Article 5 so adversaries cannot calculate how far they can go. He added that NATO has both public and undisclosed options for responding to hybrid attacks and does not have to respond with identical measures.

Kremlin Voices Openness to Trump Meeting, Pours Cold Water on Zelensky Meeting — Putin’s spokesperson claimed Putin is open to meeting Trump, a day after the latter also claimed Putin is open to meeting. But on the subject of meeting with Zelensky – which is the basis for a US-proposed trilateral meeting – the Kremlin maintains its demand that Zelensky should come to Moscow, effectively dampening any progress hailed by the US envoys after their Kyiv and Moscow visits.

‘Lifting Restrictions Must Not Become a Precedent,’ Kyiv Says After Russian Billionaires Delisted — Ukraine criticized the EU’s decision to remove Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list, warning it could weaken EU unity. But, Kyiv welcomed the bloc’s three-year extension of broader sanctions and plans new measures against Russian oligarchs.

Russia’s Jet Drone Use Explodes 8-Fold Since June, Ukraine Says — Ukraine’s air force said Russia’s use of jet-powered drones has risen drastically since June, going from 350 to 1,500 within a month, before reaching a peak of 2,850 in August. Around 1,900 launches have been documented in September so far, as Kyiv scrambles to produce enough jet-powered interceptors to meet the new challenge.

Ukraine’s Battle-Tested Drones Could Soon Be Made in America — Ukraine is ready to sign a landmark drone defense agreement with the US, CBS News reported on Tuesday, citing three people familiar with the negotiations. The framework would expand testing and production of Ukrainian military technology in America while transferring Kyiv’s battlefield expertise to US forces.

Russian Drones Over Kyiv – War of Speed and New Deep Strike Tactics — As Russia steps up its continuous attacks on civilian targets in Ukraine’s cities with increasing numbers of jet-powered Shahed drones, Ukraine is having to focus on adapting on current and future technological threats.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Drone Command Posts, Rubicon Depot in the Donetsk, Luhansk Region — Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck Russian drone command posts, a Rubicon drone depot and military supply facilities in the Donetsk and Luhansk regions, Kyiv’s General Staff said. The strikes followed a Monday attack on a Russian drone launch and storage site in Russia’s Oryol region.

Germany Probes Drone and Suspected Explosives Near Air Base — A broken drone and suspected explosive material were found near the Bundeswehr’s Wunstorf Air Base in Lower Saxony. German investigators are checking whether the discovery is connected to the attempted explosive-drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport, where Ukrainian cargo aircraft were reportedly targeted.

The EU has called recent elections there null and void and warned of steps toward possible annexation.

Stubb: ‘You Guys Are Not Going to Win This’ – Putin Must Come to the Peace Table — Finnish President said Ukraine is in a stronger position than a year ago and that Russia is not winning the war. He called for Putin to come to the negotiating table and backed a reciprocal energy ceasefire before winter.

Russian Attack on Kyiv Kills 2, Injures 22 as Gas Stations and Infrastructure Hit — Russia launched 161 drones against Ukraine overnight, damaging warehouses, gas stations and transport infrastructure in Kyiv and injuring 22, killing 2. Two people were wounded in Zaporizhzhia, while eight, including a child, were injured in Izyum by four guided bombs.

Rubio to Meet Lavrov at UN as Putin Remains Absent Since Full-Scale Invasion — Rubio and Lavrov will meet in New York on Wednesday, with Lavrov representing Moscow at the UNGA as Putin remains absent from the gathering since launching the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

7 Takeaways From Zelensky’s New York Press Conference After Trump Meeting — After meeting Donald Trump in New York, Zelensky detailed Ukraine’s energy ceasefire proposal, readiness for trilateral talks, Patriot needs, sanctions leverage and concerns over Russian pressure on Europe.

Zelensky Warns Putin May Attack NATO Country to Distract From Heavy Losses at Home — Zelensky warned that Putin could escalate against NATO countries to distract from Russia’s battlefield failures, intimidate Europe and weaken Western support for Ukraine.

US, Iran Hold First Direct Talks in Months After Trump Threatens ‘Annihilation’ — US and Iranian officials resumed face-to-face talks in New York for the first time in months, with Trump saying another meeting is planned as Tehran sets conditions for a broader deal.

Zelensky, UK Prime Minister Burnham Meet in New York as Kyiv Warns Russia Preparing Massive Attack — On the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York Zelensky and Burnham discussed air defense, winter preparations and sanctions as Kyiv warned that Russia is preparing another major attack.

Zelensky Offers Energy Truce as Trump Signals Support for Patriot Production in Ukraine — President Volodymyr Zelensky met with US President Donald Trump during the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York. Ukraine offered a reciprocal energy ceasefire should Russia halt attacks on its power grid, while Trump signaled openness to licensing Patriot interceptor production in Ukraine.

Europe Warned It Is Running Out of Time to Prepare for Wider War With Russia — Speakers at a Kyiv conference warned that Europe may already be losing the hybrid war with Russia and remains unprepared for a wider conflict. They called for stronger European defense, faster military production and a central role for Ukraine.

Hungary-Ukraine Diplomatic Relations Strain Further as Magyar Likens C8 to Village Football — Hungary’s Prime Minister Péter Magyar defended Budapest’s decision not to join Ukraine’s Carpathian Eight (C8) initiative launched on Friday, Sept. 18, which was initially presented as comprising Hungary. Trump Says Putin Is Willing to Meet as Diplomatic Momentum Continues — US President Donald Trump said Russian President Vladimir Putin is willing to meet and wants the war in Ukraine to end. Trump made his remarks during a meeting with US officials and President Volodymyr Zelensky at the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday, describing Washington’s recent efforts to broker an end to Russia’s war as productive.

Zelensky Condemns Delistings of Russian Oligarchs in Western Sanctions — During his meeting with European Commission President Ursula Von der Leyen, President Volodymyr Zelensky said proposals to remove Russian oligarchs from EU sanction lists are “suicidal and counterproductive,” linking the warning to Russia’s continued missile and drone barrage on Ukraine nationwide. The talks also centered on sustaining Ukraine’s budget and defense needs through 2027.

Erdoğan Backs Peace Upholding Ukraine’s Territorial Integrity — During the opening of the high-level debates of the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan called on Russia’s full-scale invasion to end, with Ukraine’s sovereignty and territorial integrity preserved. His statement came as Turkey remains Russia’s third-largest fossil fuel buyer.

Russia Attempts to Infiltrate Ukraine Through Pipeline from Kursk — Over the past week, Russian troops tried twice to use a major cross-border gas pipeline to penetrate northern Ukraine from Russia’s Kursk region. According to the Institute for the Study of War, both attempts failed.

Trump’s Message to Putin: ‘Settle the War’ — Speaking at the 81st United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) on Tuesday, US President Donald Trump used his address to urge an end to Russia’s war against Ukraine and warned that Washington could use new tariff powers against Moscow’s energy buyers. His remarks came ahead of a meeting with President Volodymyr Zelensky.

Commander Warns Russian Groups Could Reach Zaporizhzhia — Dmytro Filatov, commander of the 1st Separate Assault Regiment, said Russia could attempt to infiltrate Zaporizhzhia with small infantry groups during the winter. Ukraine’s Southern Grouping rejected claims that a direct Russian advance into the city is highly likely, while previous warnings about the southern front also did not lead to an assault on Zaporizhzhia.

EU to Extend Russia Sanctions After Latvia Drops Opposition to Oligarch Delistings — Latvia has backed down from opposing the delisting of two Russian oligarchs from EU sanctions, a decision pushed by France and Slovakia, ultimately paving the way for the extension of the EU’s sanctions against Russia hours before they are set to expire.

275,000 Missing in Russia-Ukraine War, Red Cross Says — About 275,000 people have been registered as missing in connection with Russia’s war against Ukraine, with the ICRC recording roughly 10,000 new cases each month.

Drone Near US Navy Air Defense Unit in Poland Prompts Polish Military 112 Call — An unauthorized drone flew near a US-operated missile defense base in northern Poland, prompting a military officer to call the emergency number 112, in accordance with procedures for incidents outside the base. Poland’s Defense Ministry said the drone remained under control and did not approach sensitive facilities.

Russia's Ex-National Guard Uniform Chief Jailed for 8 Years Over $70,000 Bribe — A Russian court has sentenced a colonel from Rosgvardiya to eight years in prison for taking a 6 million-ruble ($71,134) bribe from a contractor who never fulfilled its multibillion-ruble contract. The man is stripped of his military rank and the bribe money, in addition to receiving a court-mandated 6.7 million ruble ($79,430) fine.

Rubio Says Ukraine Targeted US-Linked Ships: What We Know — US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Ukrainian forces repeatedly targeted vessels linked to the US, possibly unintentionally. Public reporting confirms that Washington previously asked Kyiv to avoid attacks on non-Russian tankers and infrastructure connected to US energy companies, but does not show that US-flagged or US-owned ships were repeatedly hit.

India Reportedly Eyes Cut in Russian Crude Over US Sanctions Concerns — India is said to be eyeing a cut in Russian crude imports after the US signed a new sanctions bill imposing 100% tariffs on Russian oil purchasers. The US introduced similar 50% tariffs on India last year before dropping them to 18%, after which imports doubled within a month and peaked at nearly 3 million barrels per day in July, many of which made their way back to Russia as gasoline amid an ongoing fuel crisis.

Naftogaz, ORLEN Sign New LNG, $500 Million Petroleum Product Supply Deals — Naftogaz Group and its subsidiary Ukrnafta signed two memoranda with Poland’s ORLEN during the Carpathian Eight Summit, securing three LNG shipments for the first quarter of 2027 and up to $500 million in petroleum product supplies. Russian Ex-Mayor Who Left Prison for Ukraine War Dies From Combat Wounds — A former Russian mayor convicted of accepting luxury cars as a bribe was reportedly killed after signing a defense ministry contract that allowed him to leave custody and fight against Ukraine.

Molfar Intelligence Launches AI-Powered Platform to Track Information Threats — Minos brings monitoring, risk assessment, people profiling, analyst-led research and response coordination into one environment for enterprises and governments. It is built on thousands of cases worked by Molfar Intelligence analysts.

‘The World Is Bigger Than Five’ – Turkey’s Erdogan Calls for Abolition of UN Veto — Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has called for abolishing the UN Security Council’s veto and ending permanent membership, arguing the system no longer reflects today’s world. He proposed rotating elected members and a stronger General Assembly, reviving debate over a structure largely unchanged since 1945.

Ukraine's Drone Forces Hit 300 Russian Shadow Fleet Tankers in 3 Months — The commander of Ukraine’s drone forces said his branch has struck 300 Russian shadow fleet tankers within 11 weeks – 134 in the Sea of Azov and 166 in the Black Sea – in an operation dubbed “Operation MoLoChKa.” He previously put the tally at 218 struck by early August, with most vessels attacked in July, when the operation began.

Ukraine to Charge Russia in UN for Causing Humanitarian Disaster in Occupied City — Ukraine FM Sybiha urges UN intervention as Russia creates humanitarian catastrophe in occupied Oleshky (Kherson): 2,000+ civilians, incl. children, lack food, water, services; blocked aid/evacuation; people forage grass; FPV drones hunt them. Kremlin acknowledges crisis, blames Ukraine. Red Cross ready but barred.

Ukraine Hits Major Russian Drone Hub 175 Kilometers From Border, Damages 5 Launchers — Ukraine hit a Russian complex in the Oryol region used to store, prepare and launch attack UAVs, Kyiv’s General Staff said. At least three storage facilities were hit and five launchers were damaged.

Plot to Kill Russian Dissident: SBU Detains Hitwoman Sent via Belarus — Ukraine’s Security Service detained a woman accused of preparing to assassinate a Russian opposition figure who fought for Ukraine and now leads a nationwide civic organization. Putin Plans to Visit APEC Summit, May Skip Trump’s G20 — Vladimir Putin plans to attend the APEC summit hosted by Xi Jinping in China but is likely to skip Donald Trump’s G20 gathering in Florida, Bloomberg reported on Monday. Ukraine Arrests Lviv Student for Registering Starlink Terminals for Russian Troops — Ukraine said it arrested a student in Lviv and his friend for activating at least 14 Starlink terminals for Russia, and potentially at least 40 more. Ukrainian Drone Swarm Strikes Key Russian Oil Refinery in Samara — Dozens of Ukrainian drones targeted industrial facilities in Russia’s Samara Oblast overnight, reportedly striking a major Rosneft refinery and triggering a large fire, as Kyiv continues its campaign against Russia’s oil-refining infrastructure.

Russian Ballistic Strikes Hit Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad, Kill 4 — Russian forces struck industrial sites in Dnipro, Kryvyi Rih and Pavlohrad during an overnight ballistic attack, killing two and wounding three people in Dnipro.

Macron, Trump Discuss Interceptors for Ukraine and Energy Truce — Macron pressed Trump for faster missile interceptors for Ukraine and discussed a possible reciprocal moratorium on Russian and Ukrainian energy strikes.

Tsikhanouskaya Warns Against Belarus Trade as Trump Looks Beyond Canada for Potash — Sviatlana Tsikhanouskaya warned Washington against expanding trade with Minsk as Trump pursues a major Belarusian potash deal aimed at securing supplies for less than the US currently pays Canada.
